text: Şahika Ercümen (born 16 January 1985) is a Turkish dietitian and world record holder in free diving. Born in Çanakkale, she attended Gazi Primary School and completed her secondary education at Milli Piyango Anatolian High School in her hometown. She moved to Ankara for higher education and graduated from the Department of Nutrition and Dietetics at Başkent University's Faculty of Health Sciences. Her involvement in underwater sports began with scuba diving and underwater rugby, and she has been actively engaged in various underwater disciplines for twelve years, serving as a member of four national teams since 2001, including those for underwater hockey, underwater rugby, underwater orienteering, and free diving, participating in World and European Championships. On February 11, 2011, in Lake Weissensee, Austria, she achieved a 110 m (360 ft) dynamic apnea under ice (DYN), which was recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records for both men and women, surpassing the previous women's record of 70 m (230 ft) and the men's record of 108 m (354 ft). Prior to this, on November 10, 2011, in Dahab, Egypt, she set a world record in constant weight with fins at sea (CWT) at 70 m (230 ft), recognized by CMAS, previously held by Tanya Streeter at 67 m (220 ft). On the same day, she also set a CMAS-recognized record in variable weight apnea without fins at sea (VNF) at 60 m (200 ft). On June 1, 2013, she broke her own VNF record to 61 m (200 ft) in saline soda waters of Lake Van, eastern Turkey, citing her desire to highlight the migration of Pearl Mullet (Chalcalburnus tarichi), also known as Lake Van fish. On July 23, 2014, in Kaş, Antalya, southern Turkey, she reached 91 m (299 ft) in VNF in 2:49 minutes, surpassing Derya Can’s previous record. On October 22, 2016, off Kaş, Turkey, she set a new VWT record at 110 m (360 ft) in 2:44 minutes, recognized by CMAS. In a separate record, on an unspecified date, she reached 65 m (213 ft) in sweet water at Lake Salda in Yeşilova, Burdur Province, Turkey, in 1:58 minutes, surpassing the previous record of 55 m (180 ft). On October 26, 2021, in Kaş, Antalya, Turkey, she set a new VNF world record at 100 m (330 ft), valid for both women and men. In October 2025, she set a new world record in the variable weight apnea without fins at sea category, reaching 106 meters, with a dive to 107 meters under the slogan “Let Gaza breathe, let darkness turn to light” to draw attention to Gaza.
